Expect every remaining "free" lever to sit on the same frontier unless it removes pure overhead such as launches, prepare or memory traffic that carries no gradient signal.

W5 (contrarian), after E041. The tip is E036: 5.314 s. It scores 0.7532 on seeds 0–2 and 0.7525 on fresh seeds 13–22, so the population mean is about 0.7525. That is about 0.25 pp above the official 40-seed bar but below the local 3-seed gate of 0.753. To be kept, a change now has to clear the gate on seeds 0–2, so it needs either luck or an accuracy gain.

1. Exchange rate (the central fact)
- Every cut so far has cost accuracy at roughly the epoch-dial rate, about 0.07–0.1 pp per 0.1 s:
  - E033: −0.19 s, about −0.1 pp
  - E040: −0.12 s, −0.07 pp
  - E041 (12 fewer 20 px steps): −0.17 s, −0.19 pp on seeds 0–2, with noise
  - E037 (freeze at 60%): −0.25 s, −0.35 pp
  - E039 (stem BN in eval mode): −0.03 s, −0.2 pp
- Non-uniform trims did not beat uniform ones (E041 refutes H4.2.5).
- My unproposed mechanism: in a roughly 230-step run, the accuracy deficit tracks the total amount of useful optimizer updates, whatever their resolution or which layer they touch. Low-resolution and frozen-stem steps are cheap because they do less, and they buy proportionally less. Expect every remaining "free" lever to sit on the same frontier unless it removes pure overhead such as launches, prepare or memory traffic that carries no gradient signal.

2. Stem truncation is bandwidth-bound and is worth about 7 ms per truncated step (E037: 35 steps for 0.245 s).
- The cost of moving the freeze is non-linear. Train-mode group-1 BN adapting after the 28→32 px switch is my explanation for why the freeze at 75% was neutral, and it is still unresolved.
- I063 (freeze at 70%) is the clean test. I expect about −0.08 s and about −0.1 pp, so it lands on the frontier.
- I062 removes only conv1's wgrad and the pool backward, which is small.

3. Resolution
- The 20 px phase has been pushed to its limit.
- 16 px (I065) gives 1×1 final maps. At that size the max-pool head is degenerate and tensor-core use is poor, so I expect a small time gain and a disproportionate accuracy cost.

4. End-of-training boosters
- E025, E029, E030 and E032 all failed. LS and averaging tweaks are noise or harmful.
- BN recalibration (I064) is the last one. I expect +0.0 to +0.1 pp for +0.03–0.05 s.

5. Muon and fixed costs
- Muon: filter wd is inert because the filters are renormalized every step, and it already runs 3 Newton-Schulz iterations. Nothing left there.
- Fixed costs: about 0.02 s left on the mean (I066).

6. Noise
- 3-seed SD ≈ 0.15 pp; 10-seed SD ≈ 0.08 pp. Time is stable to ±0.02 s.
- "Math-identical" changes still re-roll the per-seed results through nondeterministic kernels.
- Keeps gated on held-out seeds 3–12 carry about 0.07–0.1 pp of winner's curse.

7. Strategy
- The realistic path is a +0.25-epoch top-up (+0.1 s, about +0.1 pp) paired with pure-overhead cuts (I066, launch overhead).
- Untested candidates for a better exchange rate: batch size (H5), since Muon may favour a smaller batch with more steps, and LS 0.1.
- Floor: about 5.2–5.3 s at a population mean of about 0.753.

Unsure:
- The compute vs bandwidth split (I058). I expect non-GEMM work ≥30% of a step.
- How much the PCIe judge discounts the bandwidth-bound levers.
- Whether batch 1500 gives a better rate.

forecasts.reason: No recipe change. Large 31x31 maps make BN/GELU/pool traffic big, so non-GEMM ≥30% and stem ≥35% of a 32 px step is likely.
Only conv1's wgrad and the pool backward are removed, so the saving is small (~0.03 s), and freezing conv1 15% earlier costs ~0.1 pp. It lands on the frontier and misses the gate.
~12 steps × 7 ms ≈ −0.08 s at about −0.1 pp, the usual exchange rate. A held-out mean ≥0.7545 is unlikely.
Lookahead-lerped BN stats are already roughly consistent with the averaged weights. Gain is ≤0.1 pp, below the 0.15 pp gate.
Small maps under-use tensor cores, so the saving is ~0.07 s, and 1x1 final maps carry a regime cost of ~0.15 pp.
At most ~0.02 s saved on the mean, which is close to timing noise. Accuracy stays the same or re-rolls slightly.

cruxes: Does any lever beat the ~0.1 pp per 0.1 s frontier? The test is batch 1500 under Muon (H5.1.2) or LS 0.1, measured on held-out seeds. If none does, the realistic floor is ~5.25 s.

How much of the step is pure overhead (launches, Python LR loop, per-epoch augment/interpolate/permute, Lookahead foreach) that costs no accuracy? The I058 profile should report GPU idle time and non-training kernels, not only conv vs BN.
Is the 75% freeze neutral because train-mode group-1 BN adapts after the 28→32 px switch? I063 at 70% decides whether the stem-freeze dose has any cheap room left.
